# Harden remaining exec mocks against HERDR_BIN_PATH (match herdr calls by args, not binary name)

## Problem statement

Several worklist test files use `makeExecMock` helpers that match herdr CLI calls with `bin === 'herdr'`. Because `isPaneVisible()` / pane helpers resolve the CLI as `process.env.HERDR_BIN_PATH ?? 'herdr'`, those mocks silently miss whenever the suite runs inside a herdr pane (which sets `HERDR_BIN_PATH` to an absolute path), and the call falls through to the mock's generic branch — which can flip a visibility probe to fail-open 'visible'. This is a latent hermeticity defect discovered while fixing the same issue in WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI (worklist-visibility.test.ts).

## Users

- CI agents and developers running the test suite inside herdr panes
- Automated test infrastructure that inherits `HERDR_BIN_PATH`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All 8 identified test files replace `bin === 'herdr' && …` conditions with arg-only matching (matching on `args[0]` / `args[1]` etc. only, no `bin` check), matching the pattern already applied in `worklist-visibility.test.ts`.
2. All related `makeExecMock` functions include a comment explaining why the `bin` name is not matched (referencing WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI).
3. All 8 files listed in the description plus `worklist-active-tab-marker.test.ts` are updated.
4. Full project test suite passes (`/skill:test`) with no regressions.

## Constraints

- No production code changes — test-only fix.
- Do not modify `worklist-visibility.test.ts` (already fixed).
- Preserve existing mock return shapes and behaviour.
- Keep indentation and style consistent with surrounding code.

## Existing state

The following files contain `bin === 'herdr' && …` conditions in their `makeExecMock` helpers:

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts:114` — `tab` / `get`

The fix in `worklist-visibility.test.ts` (from WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI) shows the target pattern: remove the `bin === 'herdr'` check entirely and match purely on arguments.

## Desired change

Remove `bin === 'herdr' && ` from each `if` condition in the listed files, matching the fix applied to `worklist-visibility.test.ts`. Add explanatory comments noting the hermeticity rationale.

## Key Files

# Intake Brief — Herdr: share one in-process SQLite connection per refresh to bound event-loop blocking (WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B)

## Problem statement

The default-view refresh path opens a **fresh** `WorklogDatabase` connection per `withInProcessDb` call — twice per refresh (`fetchActionableCount` + `fetchChildrenForItems` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`). Because `better-sqlite3` is fully synchronous, each open runs `new Database(...)`, WAL/foreign-key/busy-timeout pragmas, and the `initializeSchema`/`initializeFts` DDL on the **UI event loop** (~46–70 ms on the 100 MB `worklog.db`). Refreshes are occasional after the WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN counter-only-watch fix, so this is a transient pause rather than continuous lag — but when a refresh coincides with typing it breaches the ≤ 100 ms p95 input-lag budget enforced by the responsiveness guards.

## Users

- **Agent operators running the Herdr Work Items pane** — they type (search, commands, text input) in the same TUI whose event loop a refresh's synchronous DB open blocks.
  - *As an operator typing a filter, when a watch-triggered refresh lands, I want keystrokes to remain responsive (≤ 100 ms p95 input lag), so a background refresh never makes me miss a keypress.*
- **Herdr maintainers** — they must keep the input-lag budget and the no-stale-cache invariant while the fast path fans out to more read helpers.
  - *As a maintainer, I want at most one in-process connection open per refresh, so the blocking cost is bounded regardless of how many helpers the refresh fans out to.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A single in-process `WorklogDatabase` connection is opened per default-view refresh and shared by the actionable-count and expanded-children reads in that refresh; the connection is closed in a `finally` when the refresh completes.
2. No-stale-cache invariant preserved: the shared connection is still closed per refresh (never reused across a refresh boundary), so the store's in-memory query cache can never serve data across a refresh — reads always reflect the latest committed state.
3. The number of in-process DB opens per refresh drops from 2 to 1, verified by an automated test that counts opens while a refresh cycle exercises both `fetchActionableCount` and `fetchChildrenForItems`.
4. The existing responsiveness guards still pass: event-loop delay stays ≤ 100 ms p95 across watch-triggered refreshes (`worklist-watch.test.ts` F5, `hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts`), with no flakiness introduced.
5. Fallback behaviour unchanged: whenever an in-process read is not possible (no resolved worklog dir, no SQLite file, `@worklog/shared` unavailable, or an open/read error), each caller still fails open to its existing `wl` spawn path exactly as today.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the no-stale-cache invariant from WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG: never serve from the in-memory query cache across a refresh boundary — close per refresh.
- In-process reads are best-effort and fail-open: open/read failures degrade to the spawn path.
- Do not change `worklist.doRefresh`'s single-flight/trailing-refresh semantics, the typing gate (WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH), or the parallel fetch arrangement.
- Keep the lazy constructor import (`loadInProcessDbCtor`) and add no new dependencies.
- Write path and all fallback paths are untouched.

## Existing state

- `withInProcessDb` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` ~line 510) opens a fresh `WorklogDatabase` (`new Ctor(...)` — synchronous open + pragmas + `initializeSchema`/`initializeFts` DDL), runs `fn`, closes in `finally`. Two helpers use it per refresh: `fetchActionableCount` (~1005) and `fetchChildrenForItems` (~1167).
- `worklist.doRefresh` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` ~6125) calls the default fetcher, `fetchChildrenForItems`, `fetchReviewQueueState`, and later `fetchActionableCount` — so each refresh opens two in-process connections sequentially (~92–140 ms of combined blocking open cost on the 100 MB DB).
- Measured evidence: open cost ~46–70 ms each on a 100 MB `worklog.db` (including `initializeSchema`/`initializeFts`); guard budgets are filed as docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md (≤ 2 s watch→refresh, ≤ 100 ms p95 event-loop delay).

## Desired change

Open **one** in-process connection per refresh and share it between the actionable-count and children reads, closing it in a `finally` at the end of the refresh (e.g. a refresh-scoped connection object both helpers consume, or a small fetcher-level entry point). Alternative considered: move the in-process read off the critical render path entirely (worker thread / non-blocking queue) — recorded as an out-of-scope option; single shared connection is the recommended minimal change that preserves all invariants.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `withInProcessDb` (~510), `fetchActionableCount` (~1005), `fetchChildrenForItems` (~1167): add a refresh-scoped shared connection.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` (~6125): coordinate the one-open-per-refresh lifecycle (open once, share, close in `finally`).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-inprocess.test.ts` — in-process fast-path tests: add the open-count assertion (AC-3).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-watch.test.ts` — F5 event-loop-delay guard must stay green (AC-4).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — event-loop-delay guard (AC-4).
- `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` (+ `tests/bench/herdr-refresh-perf.test.ts`) — refresh benchmark; extend or reuse to confirm open count / latency.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — update the "Cold-refresh cost" section.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — refresh behaviour notes if referenced.

## Related work

- WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN — parent: *Make Herdr UI refresh snappy after agent work-item updates* (completed)
- WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG — *Cut cold refresh cost* (completed) — introduced `withInProcessDb` and the no-stale-cache invariant
- WL-0MV5CBO820024S5A — *Watch/refresh verification harness and benchmark* (completed)
- WL-0MUY1CZES0099A04 — *Herdr: UI responsiveness regression test* (completed)
- WL-0MV5CBQTS008ZWHR — *Input responsiveness regression guard* (completed)
- WL-0MSGAEPOJ002824S — *Herdr in-process memoization for identical fetches* (completed)
- WL-0MSBVYBMD004007C — *Herdr worklist: add in-flight guard to doRefresh* (completed)
- Docs: `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md`

## Assumptions & risks

- **Assumption:** sharing one open is safe for the two read helpers because they never mutate and run in the same refresh scope; verified by the open-count test.
- **Risk — subtle connection sharing bug:** a helper that still opens its own connection would silently keep the 2-open behaviour. Mitigation: the open-count assertion in AC-3.
- **Risk — test timing/flakiness:** adding an open-counter/spy must not make the responsiveness guards flaky. Mitigation: assert on open count, not wall-clock, and reuse the existing real-timer patterns from the F5 test.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the off-critical-path (worker) redesign and any connection pooling are out of scope; if they land they get their own work items. (WL-0MQPQP15S003PE9Y already covers general phase-5 pooling discussion — not re-done here.)

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MR269PDL002X882** – Impl: Retry Loop Engine with Dispatch (completed)
- **WL-0MSIG3RL1006AQID** – Wiring, fallback orchestration, lifecycle cleanup (completed)
- **WL-0MSIG3G2X007RAEL** – events.ts: HerdrEventSubscriber socket module (completed)

- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mv02va29009wben, actionable, better, blocking, blocks, bound, boundary, budget, cache, call, children, close, closing, connection, continuous, count, counter, critical, default, event, fetchactionablecount, fetchchildrenforitems, finally, fix, fresh, herdr, including, input, invariant, keep, lag, loop, memory, move, never, off, one, open, opens, operation, path, process, producer, query, read, reading, reads, refresh, refreshes, rejection, render, serve, share, sqlite, sqlite3, stale, still, store, strict, synchronous, transient, tui, twice, typing, view, watch, when, worklogdatabase

- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mv02va29009wben, actionable, better, blocking, blocks, cache, call, children, close, closing, connection, count, critical, default, event, fix, fresh, herdr, including, input, invariant, keep, lag, loop, memory, move, never, off, one, open, opens, path, process, producer, query, read, refresh, refreshes, rejection, render, serve, share, stale, still, store, transient, tui, twice, view, watch, when


## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: the item's discovery context (problem, root cause, measured open cost, recommended approach, invariant to preserve) sufficed to draft this brief. Design decision recorded — single shared connection per refresh (the seed context's proposal) is the recommended approach; the off-critical-path alternative is noted in Constraints without being selected.

# Intake Brief: Herdr audit dispatch — deepen per-window batch when the in_review queue is deep (WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS)

## Headline

Make the herdr downtime dispatcher drain a deep `completed`/`in_review` backlog faster by allowing **sequential** audit dispatches to continue within one continuous idle window (up to a small cap) whenever the audit-eligible queue depth reaches `browseItemCount`. Concurrency safety is unchanged: at most one audit is ever active, and every dispatch still passes the idle-duration gate, the ≥2 free-slot minimum, the host-wide audit marker and the per-worklog single-flight.

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher currently requires a fresh full idle period after **every** successful dispatch (`tracker.record(false)` in the worker tick), and the host-wide active-audit marker (WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA) blocks a second audit dispatch while one is running. Under sustained agent traffic, idle windows are rare, so the audit tier drains at roughly one item per idle window even when the `completed`/`in_review` queue is dozens of items deep. The audit skill can already process several items per seeded run (batch drain, SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5), but herdr only ever seeds a single-item `/skill:audit <id>` dispatch.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — wants the review queue to drain during idle compute so items reach release sooner.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deeper than my sprint window, I want the dispatcher to use one idle window for several audits (one after another) instead of one audit per window, so the backlog drains days faster without any extra LLM load.
- **Downtime dispatcher operator** — wants predictable, observable batching that never breaks the safety gates or the host-wide audit slot.
  - *User story:* As an operator, when the queue is shallow I want exactly today's behaviour, and when batching is active I want to see why each extra audit was (or was not) dispatched in the decision log.
- **Audit-tier agents** — must keep receiving one work item per dispatch and never see a duplicate or concurrent audit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Depth-aware batching: an audit-eligible depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` above 1 allows distinct audit continuations inside one idle window until the cap or the depth drop.

  Details: **Depth-aware audit batching (opt-in by depth).** When the audit-eligible backlog — root `completed`/`in_review` items that `classifyItemForDispatch` maps to `audit` (i.e. without a fresh audit and not held) — is at least `browseItemCount`, and `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (default 2, clamped, `1` = legacy/off) is greater than 1, the dispatcher may continue dispatching distinct audit targets within the same continuous idle window until the cap is reached or the depth drops below the threshold. When the depth is below the threshold, behaviour is unchanged: one dispatch per window and a fresh idle period is required before the next.

- Sequential single-audit safety: every continuation re-checks the idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention, code freeze, the active-audit markers and single-flight — no gate is relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset is deferred.

  Details: **Sequential single-audit safety.** The batch continuation never starts a second audit while one is active: it waits for the previous audit's host-wide/per-worklog marker to be released, and re-checks — on every continuation — the continuous idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention (`contention_queue_depth == 0`), the code-freeze marker, the machine-wide active-audit marker and the per-worklog single-flight. No gate is relaxed or bypassed; only the post-dispatch "require a fresh full idle period" reset is deferred for an audit-batch continuation.

- No duplicate or re-dispatched items: each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions, and any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch.

  Details: **No duplicate or re-dispatched items.** Each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions (audit id-guard, staleness-aware marker release, attempt budget, freshness/recency). A failed CAS claim, claim rollback, spawn failure, or any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the current batch rather than skipping to another target.

- Coordination-mode compatibility: the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head without releasing leadership mid-batch, and hands off leadership once at batch end.

  Details: **Coordination-mode compatibility.** On the production coordination path the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head (bounded window extension, same ranking path) without releasing leadership mid-batch; leadership hand-off still occurs once after the batch ends when the fallback was used. When the depth drops below threshold or the cap is reached, normal single-dispatch behaviour resumes immediately.

- Observability: every batch decision is recorded in the downtime decision log with a distinct reason token (`audit-batch-continue` and the existing held/blocked tokens) including depth, cap and remaining; rate limiting is unchanged.

  Details: **Observability.** Every batch decision is recorded in the existing downtime decision log with a distinct reason token (e.g. `audit-batch-continue`, and the existing tokens for held/blocked continuations), including depth, cap and remaining count. Existing reason tokens and rate limiting are unchanged.

- Test coverage in the herdr package: shallow depth keeps the single-dispatch idle reset; depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` yields N sequential audits in one idle window; idle gates, the active-audit marker, the cap, the depth drop and dispatched-marker exclusion are asserted.

  Details: **Test coverage (herdr package).** Unit tests assert: (a) shallow depth keeps today's single-dispatch behaviour including the idle-tracker reset; (b) depth ≥ `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` produces N sequential audit dispatches within one idle window; (c) an unsatisfied idle-duration gate (and sub-2 free slots) blocks all dispatch, including continuations; (d) the host-wide/per-worklog active-audit marker blocks a concurrent continuation, and continuation proceeds only after release; (e) the cap and the depth-drop are respected; (f) dispatched-marker exclusion prevents the same item being selected twice.

- Documentation: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens.

  Details: **Documentation.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

- Full suite: the full project test suite passes with the new changes, at minimum the full herdr package suite.

  Details: **Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (at minimum the full herdr package suite).

## Constraints

- Keep the strict idle-duration gate and `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` for every dispatch: reserve at least one local slot, and never fan out concurrent audits.
- The host-wide single-audit contract (WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA) remains the hard concurrency cap; this item changes only *cadence within one idle window*, never audit concurrency.
- Must not destabilise leader election/lease (5-minute TTL), coordination check-ins, pruning, fail-closed lookups, the review-queue gate, or the coordination offer path.
- Reuse `browseItemCount` (`readReviewQueueGate` / `resolveSprintViewWindow`) as the single "deep queue" threshold; do not add a second depth definition.
- The new setting is `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (settings key `downtimeAuditBatchMax`), default `2`, clamped to a safe range; `1` disables batching and restores legacy behaviour.
- No SorraAgents/audit-skill changes: the audit skill's own batch drain remains the mechanism that processes multiple items after a dispatch; herdr only decides how many audit panes to seed per window.
- Do not change the legacy `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier chain's semantics beyond the shared continuation logic; the production path is coordination mode.
- **Out of scope:** relaxing the host-wide single-audit marker, changing `AUDIT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS`/`AUDIT_BATCH_TIMEOUT` in SorraAgents, and any non-audit batching.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` consumes the Herdr list head and applies safety gates as sequential filters; `dispatchFromCoordination` (leader) dispatches at most one offer per tick and only reads its own extended head as a fallback when nothing in the offer list is dispatchable; the worker `tick()` calls `tracker.record(false)` / `perSlotTracker.record([])` after a successful dispatch, which is the per-window reset.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `readReviewQueueGate` already measures the root-only `completed`/`in_review` count against `browseItemCount` (`resolveSprintViewWindow`), and `classifyItemForDispatch` already decides whether an item is an audit candidate, including freshness/recency.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `getActiveAudit` checks the machine-wide `~/.herdr/downtime/active-audit` marker before the per-worklog dispatch-log marker; `recordDispatch` writes both, `recordPaneClose`/`recordDispatchFailure` release them.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps` wires the Herdr head, `fetchItem`, `getActiveAudit`, dispatch markers and the pane-close hooks.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — downtime settings plumbing, defaults and clamping (the new `downtimeAuditBatchMax` follows the same pattern).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — where the existing single-dispatch and audit-tier behaviour is asserted.

## Desired change

1. Add a bounded, depth-derived batch mode: compute the audit-eligible depth from the already-fetched Herdr head (root `completed`/`in_review` items are mandatory in the head), activate only when `depth >= browseItemCount` and `downtimeAuditBatchMax > 1`, and expose the remaining budget to the dispatch path.
2. In `tick()`, replace the unconditional post-dispatch idle reset with a conditional one: on a successful **audit** dispatch in active batch mode with budget remaining, keep the idle tracker armed for an audit continuation (subject to a fresh per-tick idle/slot/contention re-check); for every other dispatch, or when the budget/threshold no longer applies, preserve today's reset exactly.
3. In `dispatchFromCoordination`, allow the leader to source a continuation audit target from its own head extension after a successful batch-eligible audit dispatch, instead of only after total offer-list exhaustion; defer the own-backlog leadership hand-off until the batch ends.
4. Add `downtimeAuditBatchMax` to settings (default 2, clamped, 1 = off) and thread it through `DowntimeWorkerConfig` and the dispatch options.
5. Record `audit-batch-continue` (and held variants) in the decision log, with depth/cap/remaining metadata, at the existing rate limit.
6. Add the unit tests listed in AC6 and update the dispatcher docs/README.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — batch depth computation, continuation budget, conditional idle reset, leader continuation path, decision-log token.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `downtimeAuditBatchMax` default, parsing and clamping.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — thread the new setting into `createDowntimeWorker`/dispatch config.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` — depth-aware batch activation, cap and marker/single-flight safety tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — shallow-depth regression and idle-reset behaviour.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` — worker-loop continuation, idle gate blocking, leadership hand-off timing.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — leader own-head continuation and distinct-target guarantees.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts` — setting default/clamp coverage.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — activation rule, sequential safety invariants, decision tokens.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — operator-facing description of the new setting.

## Related work

- WL-0MT3PHW4I002SNOV — active-audit single-flight (per-worklog); preserved per item, not relaxed.
- WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA — host-wide audit serialisation; remains the hard concurrency cap.
- WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 — per-tier free-slot minimums (audit needs 2); reused unchanged.
- WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL — downtime dispatcher leader election and coordination.
- WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24 — own-backlog fallback relinquishes leadership; must be deferred to batch end.
- WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9 — sprint-view-only dispatch window (`browseItemCount` head).
- WL-0MT47BQAT00375VB — active-audit detection and audit-tier skip (per-worklog marker).
- WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9 — review-queue depth gate (same `browseItemCount` signal).
- WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD — review-queue gate rewiring (neutral `review-queue-hold`).
- SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5 (SorraAgents) — audit batch drain that consumes the seeded window.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: non-audit tiers could be starved** while a batch continues. Mitigation: batching applies only to audit dispatches and only while `depth >= browseItemCount`; as soon as no audit candidate remains, the normal tier/ranking resumes.
- **Risk: leadership hand-off logic regressed.** The existing own-backlog dispatch releases leadership immediately; deferring it for a batch could strand the leader if the batch never ends. Mitigation: release at batch end, on any failed continuation, and on the next tick when the cap/depth condition no longer holds; cover with an orchestrator test.
- **Risk: the idle-reset change leaks into other kinds.** Mitigation: scope the conditional reset to the audit-batch continuation flag only; add a regression test asserting non-audit dispatch still resets the tracker.
- **Risk: extra `wl` reads per tick hurt latency.** Mitigation: derive depth from the already-fetched head; no new subprocess in the common path.
- **Risk: a continuation starts during a code freeze or after the queue drops.** Mitigation: re-read the freeze marker and re-compute depth on every continuation tick; any frozen/ambiguous state or depth < threshold simply ends the batch and restores normal behaviour.
- **Assumption:** `completed`/`in_review` root items are mandatory-always in the Herdr head, so the head is a complete depth source up to `browseItemCount` and beyond (the existing window extension covers overflow).
- **Assumption:** the host-wide marker is released when the audit pane closes (`recordPaneClose`) or a spawn fails, so a continuation can start promptly without weakening the marker's stale window.
- **Assumption:** a sequential audit batch is acceptable to the audit runner's host-wide `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1` slot because at most one audit pane is active at a time.
- **Scope-creep risk:** relaxing host-wide serialisation (option B) or changing `AUDIT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS` (option C) is explicitly out of scope; if either becomes necessary it should be raised as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (mechanism):** How should "more than one audit per window" work — (A) keep exactly one active audit and continue sequentially within a continuous idle window, (B) dispatch N audit panes in one tick, or (C) seed the audit skill's batch queue with N ids?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(A)** — keep exactly one active audit; when depth ≥ threshold, skip the fresh-idle-period reset so the next audit dispatches once the previous audit pane closes and slots are idle again.
  - **Evidence:** host-wide active-audit marker semantics (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` § Host-wide audit serialisation) and `tick()`'s post-dispatch `tracker.record(false)`.
- **Q2 (threshold):** Reuse `browseItemCount` or add a dedicated threshold?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **Reuse `browseItemCount`** as the single deep-queue signal; add only the small cap `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (default 2).
  - **Evidence:** `readReviewQueueGate`/`resolveSprintViewWindow` already define "deep" for the review-queue gate.
- **Q3 (second target source):** Where should the extra audit target(s) come from in coordination mode?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(A)** the leader re-reads its own Herdr head after the first dispatch (extend the existing own-backlog fallback).
  - **Evidence:** `dispatchFromCoordination`'s own-backlog fallback (`getHerdrListHead` + `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`) and WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24.

## Problem statement

`.pi/test-config.json` declares the full suite as `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` + `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. Child sessions work around this with ad-hoc `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` runs, which bypass the test skill's sanctioned runner and cache — so the audit cannot see the evidence and a red herdr tree can be pushed to `dev` undetected (WL-0MVFRALLB0065UIW was caught only by a direct vitest run).

## Users

- **Herdr work-item developers** (e.g. WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS AC6/AC8) — need a sanctioned, cache-recording way to run the herdr suite.
  - *User story:* As a herdr work-item developer, when I need to verify herdr changes, I want `run_tests.py --type herdr` to run the package suite and record a cache entry, so the audit can see my evidence without me invoking vitest ad hoc.
- **Producer / reviewer** — wants gate behaviour documented and evidence visible.
  - *User story:* As a producer, I want the documentation to state which suites the dev-push gate runs and how to run the herdr suite, so gate expectations are no longer ambiguous.
- **Implement skill** — wants changed-scope selection to pick the herdr suite for herdr-touching items.

# Intake Brief — Herdr extension unresponsive on larger worklog databases (WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W)

## Problem statement

The Herdr Work Items pane freezes or visibly lags when it refreshes, is slow to
initially appear, and is slow to reflect some changes after agent writes —
problems that scale with the size of the worklog database. On a ~100 MB /
2,600-item worklog the pane's refresh path still spawns slow, memory-hungry
`wl` CLI processes (`wl worklist` ≈ 1 s / 1.2 MB JSON cold; `wl list` subsets
0.5–0.9 s each peaking ~130–145 MB; per-expand `wl dep list` ≈ 0.4 s) and the
auto-sync may spawn a ~36 s `wl sync` every 60 s. Recent fixes (event-driven
refresh, consolidated `wl worklist`, hydrator timeouts) improved the picture but
the extension remains sluggish — "improved but still not good enough".

## Users (example user stories)

- **Agent operators running the Herdr Work Items pane** — the primary user.
  - *As an operator, when the pane auto-refreshes, I want the UI to stay
    responsive (no multi-second freezes, keystrokes accepted promptly) so my
    monitoring flow is uninterrupted.*
  - *As an operator on a large worklog, when an agent writes to a work item, I
    want the pane to reflect the change within a couple of seconds so I can
    trust the list is current.*
  - *As an operator, I want the pane to open promptly and not feel like the
    extension is a drag on my machine even at 100 MB+ worklog scale.*

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Pane stays responsive during refresh:** a default-view refresh does not block the TUI event loop for more than ~200 ms of perceived lag in aggregate (verified with an automated test harness or measured timing on a large fixture DB) — keystrokes/commands process promptly while a refresh is in flight.
- **Single-figure refresh cost on large DBs:** a default-view refresh end-to-end (event → data load → render) is bounded to ≤ ~1.5 s wall-clock p95 on a DB of ~2,600 items / ~100 MB, including per-expand child fetches; the consolidated `wl worklist` single-read path stays the norm — no regression to multi-spawn refreshes.
- **Auto-sync cannot stall the pane:** while a long `wl sync` (measured ~36 s on the 100 MB DB) is in flight in the background, the pane remains responsive — no lock wait, no event-loop stall, at most a brief non-blocking status notice.
- **Change reflection latency:** after a `wl` write, the pane reflects the change within ~2 s p95 via the event-driven watch path at large-DB scale.
- **Reduced memory footprint:** a refresh's spawned `wl` processes peak at no more than a documented per-spawn budget below the ~130–145 MB/spawn observed baseline, OR concurrent spawns are bounded so aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g. ≤ ~300 MB).
- **No regressions:** the full Herdr plugin + TUI test suites pass; the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee and event-driven watch semantics are preserved.
## Constraints

- Must preserve the existing event-driven refresh, in-process SQLite read
  scopes, consolidated `wl worklist` single-read default view, and
  zero-spawn-when-idle guarantees (documented in
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`).
- Must not change the hydrator's core behaviour or the scheduler's sequential
  dispatch model without a separate work item.
- Fixes must target "large worklog" scale (100 MB+/2,600+ items) without
  regressing small worklogs.
- No new heavy dependencies; prefer reuse of the existing in-process SQLite
  read path (`@worklog/shared` `WorklogDatabase`) over new spawns.

## Existing state (measured)

- `.worklog/worklog.db` ≈ 109 MB, ~2,631 items, read cache 81 MB / ~709 entries
  (this repo).
- `wl worklist --json`: ≈ 1.0 s cold, ~1.2 MB payload.
- `wl list` (each of the four subsets): 0.5–0.9 s, peak ~130–145 MB RSS.
- `wl next`: ≈ 0.6 s. `wl dep list`: ≈ 0.4 s per call.
- `wl sync`: ≈ 36 s on this DB; auto-sync spawns fire-and-forget every 60 s
  (single-flight + heartbeat skip across panes).
- Herdr pane refresh: 30 s auto tick + event-driven (≤ ~150 ms debounce),
  single consolidated `wl worklist` read for the default view; in-process
  SQLite reads for actionable counts / child fetches within a refresh scope.
- Previous unresponsiveness work completed: WL-0MMNZWOZ60M8JY6E (TUI
  unresponsive, critical), WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P (hydrate timeouts), WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN (snappy event-driven refresh), WL-0MQFRY8TM006DIJ6 (wl next perf), WL-0MQOIBGIR006CWLR (background task runtime), WL-0MSGAEPOJ002824S / WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG (memoization + in-process reads), WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78 (consolidated worklist read).

## Desired change

Investigate the remaining large-DB cost drivers in the Herdr refresh path and
shave them down to the acceptance criteria above. Known candidates (to confirm
during implementation):

1. **Auto-sync `wl sync` cost (~36 s):** profile why `wl sync` is so slow on a
   100 MB DB (git operations, JSONL export, DB compaction?) and either bound it
   or restructure so the pane never waits on / competes with it.
2. **`wl list`/`wl worklist` RSS (~130–145 MB/spawn):** confirm where the
   memory goes (full JSON materialisation? enrichments?) and consider streaming
   or trimming payloads; cap concurrent spawns.
3. **Per-expand `wl dep list` / `wl list --parent` spawns:** replace with
   in-process SQLite reads (via the existing refresh scope) so expanding nodes
   doesn't spawn more slow processes.
4. **Event-loop blocking:** ensure every remaining spawn is off the TUI event
   loop and each refresh's in-process SQLite work stays within the one-open
   refresh scope (no per-helper DB opens).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — consolidated worklist read, in-process
  read scope, CLI exec/timeouts, spawn cap.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — background `wl sync` spawn/heartbeat.
- `src/sync.ts` / `src/commands/sync.ts` — `wl sync` pipeline (JSONL export,
  git push) — the main suspected ~36 s cost.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — refresh orchestration, guarded refresh,
  child-fetch on expand.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — the consolidated read command (payload size).
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — list/query paths used by these reads.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — per-item `wl dep list` calls (bounded by
  hydrator timeout work but still per-item spawns).

## Related work

- **WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P** — Hydrate task timeouts cause HERDR UI to become
  unresponsive (completed, high) — parent context for UI responsiveness.
- **WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN** — Make Herdr UI refresh snappy after agent work-item
  updates (completed, high) — event-driven refresh; AC 4 re-verification.
- **WL-0MNAGHQ33005BVY6** — TUI slow-down investigation (completed).
- **WL-0MMNZWOZ60M8JY6E** — TUI unresponsive to keyboard input (completed,
  critical).
- **WL-0MQFRY8TM006DIJ6** — Investigate wl next performance bottlenecks
  (completed, high).
- **WL-0MSNIX4V60012266** — Compress herdr plugin meta-data (completed) —
  vertical space, not to be confused with data-size perf.
- **WL-0MQOIBGIR006CWLR** — Background Task Runtime for non-blocking ops
  (completed, high).
- **WL-0MT1KJNGA006EEHU** — Memory pressure monitoring (completed, high).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the ~36 s `wl sync` is dominated by git push/network or JSONL
  export; fixing it may belong to a separate `wl sync` perf item (scope-creep
  guard: record a linked child, don't absorb).
- **Risk:** memory-per-spawn may be inherent to the current `better-sqlite3` +
  full-JSON payload; trimming payloads could change the fetcher contract —
  needs care to preserve the documented `wl worklist` payload stability.
- **Risk:** in-process SQLite reads on a 100 MB DB can themselves be slow
  (open + FTS DDL ~46–70 ms); the one-open-per-refresh scope must be kept.
- **Assumption:** the operator's "large DB" ≈ 100–200 MB / 2,600+ items

## Background

Parent WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W needs measurable, repeatable evidence for its ACs

This item builds the verification foundation first (test-first), reusing the
ratchet/baseline pattern proven in WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN (startup import-budget

# F3 — Auto-sync isolation: pane never stalls on `wl sync`

## Background

Auto-sync spawns `wl sync` (≈ 36 s on a ~100 MB DB) fire-and-forget every 60 s.
Parent AC 3 requires that while a long sync is in flight the pane stays
responsive: no lock wait, no event-loop stall, no "hanging" indication beyond a
brief non-blocking status notice. The current single-flight + heartbeat +
`--if-idle` guards (auto-sync.ts) bound spawns but do not yet guarantee the
pane never competes with or waits on a long-running sync (IO contention with
refresh reads, process-group/PID effects, no UI notice). F2 profiles where the
~36 s goes and whether a `wl sync` fix is a separate item (scope guard).

## Target outcome

A refresh completes within budget while a long `wl sync` is in flight in the
background, with a non-blocking status notice shown; the pane never waits on
the sync lock or its process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a simulated/hooked long ~36 s `wl sync` in flight (F1 harness), a
  concurrent default-view refresh completes within the parent AC 2 budget and
  blocks the TUI event loop ≤ 200 ms aggregate (parent AC 1); asserted by an
  automated test in the default suite.
- The auto-sync spawn is verified off the TUI event loop and the pane shows a
  non-blocking status notice ("syncing…") that never blocks input; no "hanging"
  UI state beyond the notice (parent AC 3).
- No lock contention: an in-flight sync does not hold/reset the same SQLite
  handle or filesystem lock the pane's in-process refresh scope uses; a refresh
  never waits for a sync to finish (asserted with in-flight instrumentation:
  e.g. start time monotonic, no wait gap equal to remaining sync time).
- Existing guarantees preserved: single-flight, cross-pane heartbeat skip,
  `--if-idle`, 60 s interval, no concurrent sync spawns (parent AC 6); the F1
  zero-spawn-when-idle assertion still passes.
- If F2 concludes a `wl sync` perf fix is a separate work item, this item stays
  limited to pane-side isolation and references that item — no scope creep.

## Minimal Implementation

- Route auto-sync through the same background-task runtime used elsewhere
  (`packages/herdr/src` background helpers) with explicit event-loop decoupling
  and a tiny status model the pane renders without blocking.
- Add in-flight instrumentation (process start + PID + elapsed) so a refresh
  can verify non-interference; extend F1 harness with a "sync in flight"
  scenario.
- Add the non-blocking status notice and back it with the automated
  responsiveness test above.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — spawn path, single-flight, heartbeat.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — refresh orchestration + status rendering.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — in-flight sync scenario.

## Deliverables

- Off-loop auto-sync with status notice, in-flight instrumentation, an
  automated responsiveness-under-sync test, and updated
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` notes.

## Dependencies

- F2 profile results (plus F1 harness).

# F4 — In-process dependency and child reads on expand

## Background

Expanding a node (or hydrating its deps) performs zero `wl` spawns on the

one refresh-scoped SQLite connection, with the existing fail-open CLI fallback
unchanged for correctness edge cases.

## Background

at large-DB scale, without regressing small-DB behaviour or the consolidated
single-read default view.

  single pane during a full refresh (F1 harness, full scale) is at or below a
  documented ceiling (target ≤ ~300 MB as in parent AC 5), OR per-spawn peak is

# F6 — Single, cheap in-process SQLite open per refresh

## Background

In-process SQLite reads on a ~100 MB DB carry a non-trivial open cost (open +
pragmas + FTS DDL ~46–70 ms measured in earlier work; the one-open-per-refresh
scope from WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B exists to amortise it). Surviving per-helper
opens, read-only open DDL, and connection reuse across ticks are the remaining
levers. Parent AC 2 (≤ ~1.5 s default-view refresh p95) and AC 1 (no event-loop
stall) constrain this cost; F2 quantifies its share.

## Target outcome

A default-view refresh performs at most one cheap in-process SQLite open
(shared across all refresh helpers, read-only, minimal/no DDL when already
initialised), and the open cost is small enough that it never threatens the
refresh budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An automated test (F1 harness, full scale) asserts a default-view refresh
  performs at most one in-process DB open per refresh and that helper reads
  reuse that single connection (no per-helper open).
- The read-only open path is measured and documented: open+pragmas cost is
  recorded after the change (target: eliminate the ~46–70 ms FTS-DDL hit on
  already-initialised stores, e.g. by skipping DDL when schema/version already
  present), with numbers below the refresh budget headroom.
- Open is verified off the TUI event loop / within the existing refresh scope
  (parent AC 1); any background warm-up does not overlap a visible refresh in a
  blocking way.
- Fail-open preserved: a read-only open failure degrades to the existing `wl`
  spawn fallback; no change to the hydrator's core behaviour or scheduler
  (parent constraints).
- Existing Herdr + TUI suites pass; zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent
  AC 6).

  a read-only/no-DDL mode or the skip is done at the caller.
